canton-of-aargau: Black with a wavy white line beside blue with three stars.
Its wavy line is the river that names the canton.
afghanistan: White with the Islamic declaration of faith in black script.
The tricolour it replaced in 2021 is still used at the United Nations.
Its country has had more than twenty flags since the early 20th century.
alabama: A crimson diagonal cross on a white field, nothing else.
Its sponsor wanted to preserve a feature of a Civil War battle flag.
A southern neighbour's flag adds a seal to the same design.
aland: A red cross edged in yellow on blue.
Like Sweden's flag with a red cross added.
Its islands are an autonomous, demilitarised part of Finland.
alaska: Eight gold stars on dark blue forming a famous constellation and the North Star.
Designed by a 13-year-old in a school contest.
The flag of the northernmost US state.
albania: A black double-headed eagle on red.
Based on the banner of a 15th-century commander who fought the Ottomans.
A red communist star was removed from it in 1992.
Its people's name for their country is popularly linked to the word for eagle.
alberta: A shield with mountains, foothills, prairie and wheat under St George's Cross, on blue.
Its shield shows a landscape from west to east.
algeria: Green and white vertical halves with a red crescent and star.
Its design came from a liberation front during a war of independence against France.
Its crescent's horns are unusually long.
american-samoa: Blue with a red-edged white triangle and an eagle holding a club and a whisk.
Its bird is not native to its islands.
Its symbols of chiefly authority are a fly whisk and a war club.
andalusia: Green, white and green bands with Hercules between two pillars.
Its arms show a mythical hero said to have founded the region.
andorra: Blue, yellow and red vertical bands with a quartered shield showing a mitre and two cows.
Its two co-princes are a president and a bishop.
Its motto means 'Virtue united is stronger'.
angola: Red over black with a golden half cog-wheel, machete and star.
Its emblem deliberately echoes the hammer and sickle.
A 2003 proposal to replace it with a sun design was never adopted.
anguilla: A blue ensign with three orange dolphins in a circle.
Its dolphins come from a short-lived republic declared in 1967.
Its island is named after an eel.
antigua-and-barbuda: A red flag with a V-shaped triangle holding a rising gold sun over black, blue and white.
Its colours are summed up as sun, sea and sand.
Its red sides form a V for victory.
canton-of-appenzell-ausserrhoden: A black upright bear with the letters V and R on white.
It split from its twin along religious lines in 1597.
canton-of-appenzell-innerrhoden: A black upright bear on white, without letters.
The last Swiss canton to give women the vote.
aragon: Four red stripes on gold with a quartered shield.
Its stripes belonged to a medieval crown.
argentina: Light blue and white horizontal bands with a golden sun with a face.
Its sun has 32 rays, alternately straight and wavy.
First raised by a general on the banks of the Paraná River in 1812.
Its sun recalls a revolution in May 1810.
arizona: Red and gold rays above a blue half, with a copper star in the centre.
Its central star honours a metal.
First designed for a rifle team in 1910.
arkansas: A white diamond with blue stars and the state name, on red with a star border.
Its diamond shape refers to a precious stone mined in the state.
Its 25 stars show it was the 25th state.
armenia: Red, blue and orange horizontal bands.
First adopted by a short-lived republic in 1918 and restored in 1990.
Its bottom band is sometimes said to be the colour of apricots.
aruba: Light blue with two thin yellow stripes and a red four-pointed star.
Its star's four points are the four compass directions.
Adopted in 1976 during a push for separate status.
asturias: A gold cross with hanging alpha and omega on blue.
Its cross is linked to a battle that began the Reconquista.
Its region gives the Spanish heir their title.
australia: A blue ensign with a large seven-pointed star below the canton and a constellation of white stars in the fly.
Its large star once had six points, before territories were added.
Five people with almost identical entries shared first prize in its design competition.
Its neighbour across the sea has a similar flag with red stars.
australian-capital-territory: A blue band with the Southern Cross beside white with a shield held by a black swan and a white swan.
Its swans stand for two groups of Australians.
The flag of the territory containing the national capital.
austria: Red, white and red horizontal bands of equal height.
A legend links it to a blood-stained tunic at a siege in the Third Crusade.
Its colours are recorded on a ducal seal from 1230.
A Baltic flag looks similar but with a narrower white band.
azerbaijan: Light blue, red and green bands with a white crescent and eight-pointed star.
First adopted by the first parliamentary republic in the Muslim world, in 1918.
baden-wurttemberg: Black over gold, two horizontal bands.
Its colours come from three black lions of a medieval duchy.
A German state formed in 1952 from three smaller states.
bahrain: Red with a white hoist band and a zigzag edge of five points.
Its five points stand for the pillars of a religion.
A neighbour's similar flag is maroon with nine points.
balearic-islands: Red and yellow stripes with a purple canton holding a white castle.
An island community whose capital is Palma.
bangladesh: A red disc on dark green, set slightly toward the hoist.
Its disc once contained a yellow map of the country.
First raised at a university in 1971.
Its red is both a rising sun and the blood of a liberation war.
barbados: Blue, gold and blue vertical bands with a black trident head.
Its trident's broken shaft symbolises a break from colonial rule.
Its country became a republic on its 55th independence anniversary.
canton-of-basel-landschaft: A red bishop's staff with knobs on white.
It broke away from a city in 1833.
canton-of-basel-stadt: A black bishop's staff on white.
Its country neighbour's staff is red and faces the other way.
basque-country: A green saltire and a white cross on red.
Banned under a dictatorship and legalised in 1977.
Its name means 'the flag' in the region's language.
bavaria: White and blue diamonds covering the whole flag.
Its pattern came from a dynasty that ruled for over 700 years.
A German Free State famous for Oktoberfest.
belarus: Red over green with a red and white ornamental band at the hoist.
Adopted after a 1995 referendum, replacing a white-red-white flag.
Its hoist band reproduces a traditional embroidered towel.
belgium: Black, yellow and red vertical bands, almost square.
Its colours come from a golden lion with red claws on a black shield.
First flown with horizontal stripes during an 1830 revolution.
A larger neighbour uses the same colours horizontally.
belize: Blue with red edge stripes and two men flanking a shield under a tree in a white disc.
The only national flag depicting people as its main element.
Its motto means 'Under the shade I flourish'.
benin: A green band at the hoist with yellow over red.
Its country was called Dahomey until 1975.
Replaced by a green flag with a red star and restored in 1990.
berlin: A black bear on white between two red stripes.
Its animal is a pun on the city's name.
The flag of a city-state that was divided until 1990.
bermuda: A red ensign with a lion holding a shield showing a shipwreck.
Its shipwreck may have inspired a Shakespeare play.
The only British overseas territory with a red ensign as its main flag.
canton-of-berne: A black bear on a yellow diagonal band across red.
Its animal gives the city its name, by legend.
The canton of the Swiss federal city.
bhutan: A white dragon lies across a diagonal split of yellow and orange.
Its emblem clutches jewels in its claws.
One half represents royal authority and the other a Buddhist tradition.
The creature on it is also part of the country's name in its own language.
biafra: Red, black and green bands with a golden half-sun in the black band.
Its sun's eleven rays stood for eleven provinces.
The flag of a secessionist state in West Africa in 1967–1970.
A landlocked country in south-east Africa has a similar flag with a red sun.
bolivia: Red, yellow and green horizontal bands.
A seven-coloured square patchwork flag is co-official alongside it.
Its yellow represents mineral wealth in a landlocked Andean country.
bonaire: Yellow and blue triangles divided by white, with a red star in a compass ring.
Its star's six points are six original villages.
A special municipality of a European country in the Caribbean.
bosnia-and-herzegovina: A yellow triangle on blue with a diagonal line of white stars.
Chosen by an international official after local leaders could not agree.
Its triangle is said to show the shape of the country.
Its stars are cut off at the edges to suggest they continue forever.
botswana: Light blue with a black band edged in white.
Its blue reflects a motto meaning 'rain'.
Its black and white bands are linked to a striped national animal.
brandenburg: Red over white with a red eagle on a white shield.
Its eagle belonged to the margraves who founded Prussia.
A German state surrounding the capital.
brazil: A yellow diamond on green, with a starry blue globe crossed by a white motto band.
Its stars show a real night sky from the morning a monarchy fell.
Its motto comes from a French philosopher's school of thought.
Its green and yellow came from the dynasties of an emperor and his Austrian wife.
bremen: Red and white stripes with a chequered border at the hoist.
The flag of Germany's smallest state, a Hanseatic city.
british-columbia: A Union Flag with a crown above a golden setting sun over wavy blue and white lines.
Its sun sets over the westernmost province's ocean.
Its motto plays on a sun that never sets.
british-indian-ocean-territory: Wavy blue and white stripes with a Union Flag and a palm tree over a crown.
Its islands' people were removed for a military base.
Sovereignty is being transferred to an island nation in the Indian Ocean.
british-virgin-islands: A blue ensign with a shield showing a woman in white holding a lamp, among eleven more lamps.
Its saint gave the islands their name.
brunei: Yellow with diagonal white and black stripes and a red emblem with a parasol and two hands.
Its stripes stand for two chief ministers.
Its yellow is the colour of its sultan.
bulgaria: White, green and red horizontal bands.
Adopted in 1879 after liberation from an empire.
Often said to adapt a large Slavic neighbour's tricolour, replacing blue with green.
burgenland: Red over gold, two horizontal bands.
Austria's youngest state, formerly part of Hungary.
burkina-faso: Red over green with a yellow star in the centre.
Introduced in 1984 with a new country name meaning 'land of upright people'.
Its predecessor had three bands for three branches of a river.
burundi: A white saltire with red and green triangles, and three red stars in a central white disc.
Its stars stand for three words in a national motto.
A royal drum was removed from its centre after the monarchy fell.
california: A grizzly bear on white with a red star and the words 'CALIFORNIA REPUBLIC'.
Based on the flag of a 25-day republic in 1846.
The animal on it is extinct in the wild in the state.
cambodia: A white temple on a red band between two blue bands.
The only national flag whose main emblem is a building.
Its temple appeared even on the flag of the Khmer Rouge.
cameroon: Green, red and yellow vertical bands with a yellow star in the centre.
Its two stars became one when a federation became unitary.
Its red stands for unity between north and south.
canada: Red bars on either side of a white square containing a single red leaf.
Its leaf has eleven points, chosen after wind-tunnel testing.
A heraldic term for a central square as wide as the flag is tall is named after it.
It replaced a red ensign after a long parliamentary debate in 1964.
canary-islands: White, blue and yellow vertical bands.
Its islands are named after dogs, not birds.
cantabria: White over red, two bands, from a Spanish port.
Identical in design to a European country's flag.
cape-verde: Blue with white and red stripes and a ring of ten yellow stars.
Its stars stand for ten islands.
It replaced a flag shared in style with a mainland neighbour.
carinthia: Yellow, red and white horizontal bands.
Its colours come from three black lions on gold and an Austrian shield.
castile-and-leon: Quarters of gold castles on red and purple lions on white.
It joins two medieval kingdoms united in 1230.
castilla-la-mancha: Crimson with a gold castle beside a white half.
catalonia: Four red stripes on gold, nothing else.
By legend its stripes were drawn in blood by a count's fingers.
One of the oldest flags in Europe still in use.
cayman-islands: A blue ensign with a shield showing three green stars, a lion, a turtle and a pineapple.
Its three stars are three islands rising from the sea.
Its motto comes from a psalm.
central-african-republic: Blue, white, green and yellow bands crossed by a vertical red stripe, with a yellow star.
Its colours combine French and Pan-African palettes.
It survived unchanged through a self-proclaimed empire in the 1970s.
ceuta: Black and white triangles meeting at the centre, with the arms of another country.
A Spanish city on the African coast.
chad: Blue, yellow and red vertical bands.
Almost identical to a European flag.
Its blue replaced green to avoid matching its neighbours.
chile: White over red with a white star on a blue canton.
Often mixed up with a US state flag that has a vertical blue band.
Its white band stands for the snow of a mountain range.
First flown at its declaration of independence in 1818.
china: Red with one large yellow star and four smaller stars curving around it.
Its smaller stars each point toward the large one.
A hammer and sickle was removed from its design before adoption in 1949.
Designed by an economist who entered a national competition.
christmas-island: Blue and green diagonal halves with the Southern Cross, a golden bird and a map in a yellow disc.
Its island is known for its red crab migration.
Named after the day it was sighted in 1643.
cocos-keeling-islands: Green with a yellow palm, a crescent and the Southern Cross in yellow.
Its islands were once owned by a single family.
Its crescent represents a Muslim majority.
colombia: Yellow on the top half, then blue and red bands below.
Its colours were first flown by a revolutionary who reportedly discussed colour theory with Goethe.
Two neighbours, all once part of a union led by Bolívar, use the same colours.
Its blue band is said to represent two oceans.
colorado: Blue and white bands with a red letter C around a gold disc.
Its letter stands for its name and the year 1876.
One of the most recognisable US state flags in branding.
community-of-madrid: Its stars form a famous constellation.
The flag of the region around Spain's capital.
comoros: Four stripes with a green hoist triangle holding a white crescent and four stars.
Each stripe stands for an island, including one it does not control.
Its flag has changed many times since 1975.
connecticut: A white shield with three grapevines on blue, with a Latin motto.
Its vines are said to be three early settlements.
Its motto means 'He who transplanted still sustains'.
cook-islands: A blue ensign with a circle of fifteen white stars.
Its stars stand for fifteen islands.
Its islands are in free association with a Pacific neighbour.
costa-rica: Blue, white, double-height red, white and blue stripes.
Designed by a First Lady inspired by a European revolution in 1848.
An Asian kingdom's flag has the same pattern with two colours swapped.
croatia: Red, white and blue bands with a red and white chequered shield.
Its shield is topped by a crown of five smaller shields.
Its national football kit copies the shield's pattern.
cuba: Blue and white stripes with a red hoist triangle holding a white star.
A neighbouring island's flag has the same layout with reversed colours.
Designed in New York in 1849 for an expedition against Spanish rule.
Its three blue stripes stood for three military departments.
curacao: Blue with a yellow stripe below the centre and two white stars.
Its two stars are a main island and a small uninhabited one.
Its blue is both sky and sea.
cyprus: A copper-orange map of an island on white, above olive branches.
Its colours were chosen to favour neither of two communities.
Its island's name is linked to a metal.
czech-republic: White over red with a blue triangle at the hoist.
Kept by one successor state despite an agreement not to.
Its triangle was added for a region that later became independent.
delaware: A light blue field with a buff diamond holding a coat of arms and the date 1787.
Its date marks the first state to ratify a constitution.
Its colours are those of a revolutionary army's uniforms.
democratic-republic-of-the-congo: Sky blue with a yellow-edged red diagonal and a yellow star in the corner.
Its star goes back to a 19th-century king's private colony.
Between 1971 and 1997 its country used a green flag with a torch.
denmark: A white off-centre cross on a red field.
Legend says it fell from the sky during a battle in 1219.
Every other flag of its regional cross family is modelled on it.
Often called the oldest national flag still in continuous use.
djibouti: Light blue over green with a white hoist triangle and a red star.
Its two colours stand for two communities.
It was once called the Territory of the Afars and the Issas.
dominica: Green with a cross of yellow, black and white stripes and a parrot in a red disc.
One of only two national flags with purple.
Its ten stars stand for ten parishes.
dominican-republic: A white cross between blue and red quarters, with a shield holding an open book.
The only national flag that shows a Bible.
Its design added a white cross to a neighbour's colours.
east-germany: Black, red and gold bands with a hammer and compass in a wreath of grain.
Protesters in 1989 cut holes in its centre.
For its first ten years it was identical to its western neighbour's flag.
Its emblem stood for workers, intellectuals and farmers.
ecuador: Yellow (double width), blue and red bands with a condor-topped coat of arms.
Its arms show a snow-capped volcano and an early steamship.
Without its arms, it closely resembles a neighbour's flag.
Zodiac signs on it mark the months of an 1845 revolution.
egypt: Red, white and black horizontal bands with a golden eagle in the centre.
Its eagle is named after a 12th-century sultan.
Between 1958 and 1971 it showed two green stars from a short-lived union.
Its colours came from a revolution in 1952.
el-salvador: Blue, white and blue bands with a triangular emblem of five volcanoes and a liberty cap.
Its emblem's text names its country 'in Central America'.
From 1865 to 1912 it used a flag copied from the US.
england: A red centred cross on white, nothing else.
Its saint is said to have slain a dragon.
It forms part of a union flag.
equatorial-guinea: Green, white and red bands with a blue hoist triangle and a tree under six stars.
Its six stars are the mainland and five islands.
eritrea: A red triangle spanning the flag between green and light blue triangles, with a gold olive wreath.
Its wreath's leaves are said to count the years of a war of independence.
Its olive emblem came from a 1950s federal flag.
estonia: Blue, black and white horizontal bands.
It began as a students' society flag in a university town in 1884.
It was raised again on a medieval tower in its capital in 1989.
eswatini: Blue, yellow and crimson stripes with a horizontal black and white shield and spears.
Based on a banner given to a wartime pioneer corps.
Its country changed its English name in 2018.
ethiopia: Green, yellow and red bands with a yellow star of lines on a blue disc.
Its colours became the Pan-African colours because the country was never colonised.
A lion holding a staff was removed from its centre after a 1974 revolution.
A religious movement in Jamaica reveres its former emperor and uses its colours.
extremadura: Green, white and black horizontal bands with a shield.
falkland-islands: A blue ensign with a ram on grass above a sailing ship.
Its motto is a pun on a ship's name.
Its islands were fought over in 1982.
faroe-islands: A red Nordic cross edged in blue on white.
Designed by students in 1919, recognised during wartime occupation.
Like Norway's flag with its red and white swapped.
federated-states-of-micronesia: Four white stars in a diamond on light blue.
Its stars stand for four island states.
Its predecessor had six stars for six districts.
fiji: A light blue ensign with the Union Flag and a shield showing a lion, sugar cane, a palm and a dove.
A plan to remove its Union Flag was dropped after an Olympic rugby victory.
Its shield shows bananas and a coconut palm.
finland: A blue Nordic cross on a white field.
A poet described its colours as lakes, sky and snow.
Adopted in 1918 after independence from an empire.
On its Flag Day, flags fly all night at midsummer.
florida: A red saltire on white with a seal showing a woman, a palm and a steamboat.
Its saltire was added so it would not look like a surrender flag.
Its neighbour's flag is the same saltire without a seal.
france: A vertical tricolour with blue at the hoist and red at the fly.
The colours of its capital city were combined with the white of a royal dynasty during a revolution.
Its navy flies a version with unequal stripes so it looks even in the wind.
Decreed by a revolutionary assembly in 1794, it was banned for fifteen years after an emperor's fall.
french-polynesia: Red and white bands with a canoe of five figures over a sun and waves.
Its five paddlers are five archipelagos.
Its red and white come from a 19th-century island kingdom.
canton-of-fribourg: A bilingual canton that joined in 1481.
gabon: Green, yellow and blue horizontal bands.
Its yellow stands for the equator, which crosses the country.
A French tricolour was removed from its canton at independence.
galicia: A single blue diagonal band on white.
It came from a port's maritime flag.
The region of Santiago de Compostela.
canton-of-geneva: Half a black eagle on yellow beside a gold key on red.
Its city hosts the Red Cross and UN offices.
georgia-united-states: Red-white-red bands with a blue canton holding a ring of thirteen stars around an arch.
Based on the first Confederate national flag.
Shares its name with a country in the Caucasus.
georgia: A large red cross on white with four smaller red crosses in the quarters.
Adopted after a revolution named after a flower in 2003.
A version is shown on a 14th-century map at the city of Tbilisi.
Its large cross is that of the nation's patron saint.
german-empire: Black, white and red horizontal bands.
It combined the colours of a kingdom with those of a league of trading cities.
Chosen by a chancellor who rejected the colours of the 1848 revolution.
It was abandoned in 1918, briefly restored in 1933 and dropped again in 1935.
germany: Three horizontal bands: black on top, then red, then gold.
Its colours trace back to the uniforms of a volunteer corps that fought Napoleon.
A revolutionary parliament adopted it in 1848, but it became official only in 1919.
For forty years two neighbouring states used it, one with a hammer and compass added.
ghana: Red, gold and green horizontal bands with a black star in the middle.
Its star gives a national football team its nickname.
The first flag of an independent sub-Saharan African colony, from 1957.
For two years its middle band was white under a one-party state.
gibraltar: White with a red castle and a gold key, and a red band along the bottom.
Its arms were granted by a Castilian queen in 1502.
Its key represents the entrance to a sea.
canton-of-glarus: A walking monk with a staff on red.
The only Swiss cantonal flag showing a person.
Its figure is an Irish missionary saint.
canton-of-the-grisons: A flag combining three historic leagues, with an ibex.
Switzerland's largest canton, with three official languages.
greece: Nine blue and white stripes with a white cross in a blue canton.
Its stripes are often linked to the syllables of a revolutionary motto.
For 150 years it was only the sea flag; a plain cross flag was used on land.
Its shade of blue has never been fixed by law.
greenland: White over red with a half-red, half-white disc.
The only Nordic flag without a cross.
Its disc is the sun setting over an ice cap.
grenada: A red border with stars around yellow and green triangles, with a nutmeg near the hoist.
The only national flag with a spice on it.
Its country is called the 'Isle of Spice'.
guam: Dark blue with a red border and a pointed oval seal showing a palm and a canoe.
Its seal is shaped like a sling stone.
Its word in red letters is the territory's name.
guatemala: Sky blue and white vertical bands with a long-tailed green bird on a scroll.
Its scroll gives a date in September 1821.
Its bird is also the name of the country's currency.
guernsey: St George's Cross with a gold cross inside it.
Its gold cross is linked to William the Conqueror.
Its gold was added because it was identical to England's flag.
guinea: Red, yellow and green vertical bands.
Its colours match a motto of Work, Justice, Solidarity.
Its country was the first French colony in Africa to vote 'No' to the French Community.
guinea-bissau: A red hoist band with a black star, beside yellow over green.
Its design came from a liberation party shared with an island nation.
Independence was declared months after its leader was assassinated.
guyana: A yellow arrowhead and red triangle edged in white and black on green.
Designed by the man who coined the word 'vexillology'.
haiti: Blue over red with a palm tree and liberty cap on a white square.
Created by tearing the white out of a colonial power's tricolour.
hamburg: A white three-towered castle on red.
The flag of Germany's second-largest city.
A Hanseatic city-state with a famous port.
hawaii: Eight white, red and blue stripes with the Union Flag in the canton.
The only US state flag containing another country's flag.
Its stripes stand for eight islands of a former kingdom.
hesse: Red over white, two horizontal bands.
Its colours come from a lion with red and white stripes.
A German state containing a major financial centre.
honduras: Blue, white and blue bands with five blue stars arranged like an X.
Its stars represent the five states of a former federation.
Its shade of blue changed in 2022.
hong-kong: Red with a white five-petalled flower, each petal holding a red star.
Raised at a handover from Britain in 1997.
Its flower is a sterile hybrid first found in the territory.
hungary: Red, white and green horizontal bands.
In 1956 protesters cut the emblem out of its centre.
Its colours come from royal stripes and a triple mount in a coat of arms.
Turn it vertical and you get a southern European flag.
iceland: A red cross edged in white on a blue field.
Its colours officially stand for mountains, ice and volcanic fire.
An earlier unofficial version was rejected partly for resembling a Mediterranean flag.
A nearby kingdom uses the same pattern with two colours swapped.
idaho: A detailed seal with a woman and a miner on blue, above a red scroll.
Its seal is the only US state seal designed by a woman.
Its motto means 'Let it be perpetual'.
illinois: An eagle on a rock holding a shield and banner, on white, with the state name below.
Its name was added at a serviceman's request in 1970.
Its motto balances state sovereignty and national union.
india: Saffron, white and green horizontal stripes with a navy wheel in the middle.
Its central wheel has 24 spokes and comes from an emperor's stone pillar.
A spinning wheel was replaced by a wheel of law weeks before independence.
Its flag code once required the flag to be made from hand-spun cloth.
indiana: A gold torch on blue surrounded by nineteen gold stars.
Its largest star marks the 19th state.
Designed for a state centennial in 1916.
indonesia: Red over white, two equal horizontal bands.
Almost identical to a European principality's flag, except for proportions.
Its colours are traced to a medieval Javanese empire.
Its first copy was sewn by the wife of the country's first president.
iowa: Blue, white and red vertical bands with an eagle carrying a streamer.
Its tricolour recalls a French territory sold in 1803.
Designed for soldiers in the First World War.
iran: Green, white and red with a red central emblem and stylised script along the band edges.
A religious phrase is repeated 22 times on it, for a date in its calendar.
A lion holding a sword under a rising sun was removed from it after a revolution.
Its central emblem is shaped like a tulip.
iraq: Red, white and black bands with green Arabic script in the centre.
Its script was once in a dictator's handwriting.
Three green stars were removed from it in 2008.
Its tricolour dates from a proposed union of three Arab states in 1963.
ireland: Green, white and orange vertical bands.
Its white band was described as a truce between two religious traditions.
Presented in 1848 after its presenter received it in Paris.
It flew over a post office during an uprising in 1916.
isle-of-man: Three armoured legs joined at the centre on red.
Its motto says it will stand however it is thrown.
An Italian island's flag also has three legs.
israel: A blue six-pointed star between two horizontal blue stripes on white.
Its design was modelled on a prayer shawl.
First used at a congress held in Basel in 1897.
italy: Green, white and red vertical bands with no emblem.
First adopted by a republic created in 1797 in the north of its peninsula.
A royal shield was removed from its white band after a 1946 referendum.
Its constitution defines it in a single sentence.
ivory-coast: Orange, white and green vertical bands.
Often confused with a European flag that has the same colours in reverse.
Its orange is the northern savannah and its green the southern forest.
jamaica: A gold diagonal cross with green triangles top and bottom and black triangles at the sides.
The only national flag with no red, white or blue.
An earlier horizontal design was dropped for looking like an East African flag.
Its black triangles were once said to represent hardships.
japan: A single red circle centred on a white field, nothing else.
Its disc used to sit very slightly toward the hoist until a 1999 law centred it.
The disc evokes a goddess from whom an imperial dynasty claims descent.
jersey: A red saltire on white with a red shield of three gold lions under a crown.
Its lions come from a medieval duchy in France.
jordan: Black, white and green bands with a red hoist triangle holding a white seven-pointed star.
Its star's points refer to the verses of a chapter of the Quran.
Based on the flag of a revolt against the Ottoman Empire in 1916.
A neighbouring flag is identical except for the star.
canton-of-jura: A red bishop's staff beside seven red and white stripes.
It seceded from a larger canton after a referendum.
kansas: A seal on dark blue under a sunflower, with the state name below.
Its Latin motto means 'To the stars through difficulties'.
Its seal has 34 stars for the 34th state.
kazakhstan: A golden sun and eagle on sky blue, with an ornamental band at the hoist.
Its hoist band shows a 'ram's horn' pattern.
Adopted in 1992 after a competition, replacing a Soviet republic flag.
kentucky: A seal on navy blue with two men shaking hands, ringed by goldenrod.
Its motto is 'United we stand, divided we fall'.
Its two figures are often said to be a frontiersman and a famous senator.
kenya: Black, red and green bands with thin white stripes, and a shield and two spears in the centre.
The shield on it is of a traditional pastoralist people's design.
Its colours come from the party that led the country to independence in 1963.
kiribati: A golden frigatebird over a rising sun above wavy blue and white bands.
Its sun's rays stand for 17 islands.
Its country's name is a local form of the word 'Gilberts'.
kosovo: A gold map on blue under an arc of six white stars.
Designed to avoid any single ethnic group's symbols.
One of only two national flags that show a map of the country.
kuwait: Green, white and red bands with a black trapezoid at the hoist.
Its colours are described in a medieval line of poetry about deeds, battles, fields and swords.
It replaced a red flag bearing the country's name in 1961.
kyrgyzstan: A golden sun with 40 rays on red, holding the crown of a yurt.
Its rays stand for forty tribes united by an epic hero.
Its sun's rays were straightened in 2023 after being likened to a sunflower.
la-rioja: Red, white, green and yellow bands with a shield.
The flag of a famous wine region.
laos: Red, double-height blue and red bands with a white disc in the centre.
Its disc is the full moon over a great river.
It replaced a flag showing a three-headed elephant in 1975.
latvia: A dark carmine red flag with a narrow white horizontal stripe.
A legend says it shows a chieftain's blood-stained sheet.
A 13th-century chronicle describes a banner like it.
lebanon: A green tree on a white band between two red bands.
Its central tree touches both of the coloured bands.
Before independence its tree sat on a European tricolour.
lesotho: Blue, white and green bands with a black conical hat in the centre.
Its hat is said to resemble a mountain.
Adopted in 2006 to replace a flag showing weapons.
liberia: Red and white stripes with a single white star on a blue canton.
Its eleven stripes stand for the signers of a declaration of independence.
Modelled on the flag of the country whose freed citizens founded it.
libya: Red, black (twice as tall) and green bands with a white crescent and star.
Its predecessor was plain green, the only one-colour national flag.
A monarchy's flag revived by a 2011 uprising.
Its three colours stand for three historic regions.
liechtenstein: Blue over red with a gold crown in the upper hoist.
Its crown was added after a surprise at the 1936 Olympics.
Without the crown, it matched a Caribbean nation's flag.
lithuania: Yellow, green and red horizontal bands.
Its historical companion flag shows a mounted knight.
Its colours were chosen from traditional folk weaving in 1918.
louisiana: A white pelican feeding three chicks on blue.
Drops of blood were added to it in 2006.
Its bird comes from a medieval symbol of self-sacrifice.
lower-austria: Blue over yellow, two horizontal bands.
Its colours come from five golden eagles attributed to a saint.
The Austrian state that surrounds the capital.
lower-saxony: The German tricolour with a white horse on a red shield.
Its horse is the Saxon Steed.
A northern German state formed in 1946.
canton-of-lucerne: A square split vertically into blue and white.
The first city to join the Swiss founding cantons.
luxembourg: Red, white and light blue horizontal bands.
Almost identical to a neighbouring kingdom's flag, but longer and lighter blue.
Its colours come from a red lion on striped white and blue.
macau: Green with a white lotus over a bridge and water, under five yellow stars.
Raised in 1999 when the last European colony in Asia was handed over.
Its lotus's three petals stand for three areas of land.
madagascar: A white vertical band at the hoist with red over green.
Its red and white came from a highland kingdom conquered in 1897.
Adopted in 1958 for an island republic.
maine: A coat of arms on blue with a farmer, a sailor, a moose and a pine tree.
Voters chose to keep it over a simpler pine tree design in 2024.
malawi: Black, red and green bands with a red rising sun in the black band.
It was changed to a full white sun in 2010 and changed back in 2012.
malaysia: Red and white stripes with a blue canton holding a yellow crescent and a many-pointed star.
Its star and stripes kept a count of fourteen after one member left the federation.
Its yellow is the royal colour of its hereditary rulers.
maldives: A red field with a green rectangle containing a white crescent.
The flag of the world's lowest-lying country.
A black and white hoist band was removed at independence in 1965.
mali: Green, yellow and red vertical bands, no emblem.
A human figure was removed from it in 1961.
A neighbour's flag has the same colours in reverse order.
malta: White and red vertical halves with a small grey cross in the corner.
Its cross is a medal awarded by a king in 1942.
Its colours are linked to a Norman count and a knightly order.
manitoba: A red ensign with a shield showing a bison on a rock.
Adopted in 1966, a year after a similar neighbouring flag.
Its animal is a symbol of the prairies.
marshall-islands: Blue with orange and white diagonal stripes and a white star with 24 points.
Its stripes are two island chains named after sunrise and sunset.
Its star's points stand for 24 municipalities.
maryland: Quarters of black-and-gold stripes and red-and-white crosses.
The only US state flag based on the arms of English noble families.
Its two halves once stood for opposing Civil War sympathies.
massachusetts: A white flag with a blue shield showing a Native American and an arm with a sword above.
Its arms are under review after criticism by Native groups.
Its Latin motto speaks of seeking peace by the sword.
mauritania: Green with a gold upward-facing crescent and star, and red stripes at top and bottom.
Its red stripes were added after a 2017 referendum.
mauritius: Four equal stripes of red, blue, yellow and green.
Its island country was the home of the dodo.
Its blue stands for the surrounding Indian Ocean.
mecklenburg-vorpommern: Five stripes of blue, white, yellow, white and red.
Its colours combine two historic regions on the Baltic.
A German state with a bull's head and griffin on its arms.
melilla: A light blue field with a city coat of arms.
A Spanish city on the North African coast taken in 1497.
mexico: Green, white and red vertical bands with an eagle eating a snake on a cactus.
Its emblem retells the founding legend of a city built on a lake.
Remove its emblem and it closely resembles a European flag.
Its current emblem was redrawn just before its capital hosted the Olympics.
michigan: A coat of arms on blue with an elk and a moose supporting a shield, and an eagle above.
Its motto invites you to look around for a pleasant peninsula.
minnesota: A white eight-pointed star in a dark blue shape against light blue.
Adopted in 2024 after a public redesign commission.
Its star refers to a French state motto, 'Star of the North'.
mississippi: A white magnolia in a ring of stars on blue, between red bands edged in gold.
It replaced a flag with a Confederate battle emblem in 2021.
Its gold star honours Native American heritage.
missouri: Red, white and blue bands with a coat of arms with two bears in a ring of 24 stars.
Its stars show it was the 24th state.
Its arms show the Roman numerals for 1820.
moldova: Blue, yellow and red vertical bands with an eagle holding a cross.
Its shield shows the head of an extinct wild ox.
Remove the emblem and it matches its western neighbour's flag.
monaco: Its colours come from the arms of a family that has ruled since the 13th century.
An Asian country's flag is almost identical.
mongolia: Red, blue and red vertical bands with a golden column of symbols at the hoist.
Its emblem was created by a 17th-century monk as part of an alphabet.
A communist star was removed from it in 1992.
Its central blue represents the 'eternal blue sky'.
montana: A seal with mountains, falls and mining tools on blue, under the state name.
Its motto in Spanish means 'Gold and Silver'.
Based on a flag carried in the Spanish–American War.
montenegro: A gold-bordered red flag with a crowned golden double-headed eagle.
Its eagle has a lion on its breast.
Adopted two years before its country left a union in 2006.
montserrat: A blue ensign with a woman in green holding a harp and a cross.
Its island is called 'the Emerald Isle of the Caribbean'.
Saint Patrick's Day is a public holiday there.
morocco: A green interlaced star on a red field.
Its star was added in 1915 because plain red flags were confused at sea.
Its star is known by the name of a biblical king.
Its red is linked to a royal dynasty.
mozambique: A red hoist triangle with a star, a book, a hoe and a rifle.
The only national flag that shows an assault rifle.
Green, black and yellow bands edged in white, inherited from a liberation movement.
myanmar: Yellow, green and red bands with a large white star across them.
Introduced in 2010 under a military-drafted constitution.
Its predecessor had a cogwheel and rice plant in the canton.
Its colours echo a wartime flag that featured a peacock.
namibia: A red diagonal band edged in white, with a sun in the blue triangle and green below.
Adopted in 1990 at independence from a neighbour's administration.
Its gold sun recalls a coastal desert.
nauru: Dark blue with a thin gold line and a white twelve-pointed star below it.
Its stripe is the equator and its star the island just south of it.
Its star's points stand for twelve tribes.
navarre: Gold chains with an emerald under a crown, on red.
Its chains are linked by legend to a battle in 1212.
The region of the running of the bulls.
nebraska: A gold and silver seal on blue with a blacksmith, a cabin, a steamboat and a train.
Its motto is 'Equality before the law'.
It was a state banner before becoming the state flag in 1963.
nepal: The only national flag that is not a rectangle.
Two stacked crimson pennants with a blue border.
A white moon above and a white sun below.
Its constitution gives step-by-step geometric instructions for drawing it.
netherlands: Red, white and blue horizontal stripes of equal height.
Its top stripe was originally orange, after a princely house.
On royal holidays an orange pennant is flown above it.
A neighbouring grand duchy has a nearly identical flag with a lighter blue.
canton-of-neuchatel: Green, white and red vertical bands with a small white cross.
A canton that was once ruled by the King of Prussia.
nevada: Cobalt blue with a silver star in sagebrush and a gold 'Battle Born' scroll.
Its scroll says it became a state during a civil war.
Its star honours a precious metal.
new-brunswick: A gold lion on red above an oared ship on waves.
new-caledonia: Blue, red and green bands with a yellow disc holding a black carved spire.
Its spire tops traditional Kanak houses.
It flies alongside a European tricolour.
new-hampshire: A seal showing a ship under construction, ringed by laurel and nine stars on blue.
Its nine stars mark the ninth state to ratify the Constitution.
Its ship is a Revolutionary War frigate.
new-jersey: A coat of arms with two goddesses and three ploughs on a buff field.
Its unusual colour was ordered by George Washington for uniforms.
new-mexico: A red sun symbol with four groups of rays on yellow.
Its symbol comes from a pueblo's pottery.
Often voted the best-designed US state flag.
new-south-wales: A blue ensign with a red cross on white, with a gold lion and four gold stars.
The flag of the oldest Australian colony.
Its four stars represent the Southern Cross.
new-york: A coat of arms with Liberty and Justice and a sun rising over a river, on blue.
A crown lies discarded at one figure's feet.
new-zealand: A blue ensign with four red stars edged in white.
It survived a 2016 referendum against a silver-fern design.
Its neighbour's very similar flag has white stars and an extra seven-pointed star.
A flag chosen by Māori chiefs in 1834 preceded it.
newfoundland-and-labrador: White with blue triangles at the hoist and a gold arrow with red triangles in the fly.
Designed by a painter in 1980 to replace the Union Flag.
Its fly shapes together suggest a trident.
nicaragua: Blue, white and blue bands with a triangle of five volcanoes under a rainbow.
Its rainbow makes it one of only two national flags with purple.
Its emblem names its country and 'América Central'.
canton-of-nidwalden: A white double key on red.
Half of a founding canton, sharing a key symbol with its twin.
niger: Orange, white and green horizontal bands with an orange disc, nearly square.
Its orange stands for a vast desert.
Often confused with a large Asian country's flag that has a wheel.
nigeria: Green, white and green vertical bands.
Designed by a student in London; the judges removed a sun from the centre.
Raised at midnight at independence in 1960.
Its colonial predecessor showed a six-pointed star around a crown.
niue: Yellow with a Union Flag canton holding five yellow stars.
The only flag with a Union Flag on a yellow field.
norfolk-island: Green, white and green vertical bands with a pine tree in the centre.
Many of its residents descend from mutineers.
Like Nigeria's flag with a tree added.
north-carolina: A blue hoist band with a star and the letters N C, beside red over white, with two dated scrolls.
One of its dates refers to a declaration whose existence is disputed.
Its other date marks the first colony to call officially for independence.
north-dakota: A bald eagle with a scroll and stars on blue with gold fringe, and the state name below.
It copies an infantry regiment's flag.
Its proportions are taller than most.
north-korea: A broad red stripe edged in white between blue bands, with a red star on a white disc.
It replaced a yin-yang flag in 1948 on Soviet advice.
A village near the border flies it from an enormous flagpole.
north-macedonia: A yellow sun with eight rays spreading to the edges of a red field.
It replaced a 16-rayed star flag after a dispute with a southern neighbour.
Its sun is the 'new sun of liberty' from its national anthem.
north-rhine-westphalia: Green, white and red bands with arms showing a river, a horse and a rose.
Its colours combine the Rhineland and Westphalia.
northern-cyprus: White with two red stripes and a red crescent and star.
A giant copy is painted on a mountainside facing a divided capital.
northern-mariana-islands: Blue with a white star over a grey stone pillar in a flower wreath.
Its stone pillar is from ancient Chamorro houses.
northern-territory: A black band with the Southern Cross beside an ochre field with a desert flower.
The only Australian state or territory flag without the Union Flag.
Its ochre reflects the colour of the land.
northwest-territories: Blue and white vertical bands with a shield showing a fox's head and a wavy line.
Its shield marks the tree line between forest and tundra.
A new territory was carved from it in 1999.
norway: A blue cross edged in white on red, offset toward the hoist.
Designed in 1821 by adding a blue cross to a neighbour's flag.
Its colours were chosen as colours of liberty, after three revolutionary-era nations.
A nearby island nation uses the same pattern with its colours swapped.
nova-scotia: A blue saltire on white with a red lion on a gold shield.
Like Scotland's flag with colours reversed.
nunavut: Gold and white halves with a red stone figure and a blue star.
Its stone figure is a traditional landmark of the Inuit.
The flag of a territory created in 1999.
canton-of-obwalden: Red over white with a key in counterchanged colours.
Its key belongs to Saint Peter.
ohio: A swallowtail pennant with stripes, a blue triangle and a white O around a red disc.
The only non-rectangular US state flag.
Its circle stands for a letter and a nut.
oklahoma: A buffalo-hide shield with eagle feathers, a peace pipe and an olive branch on sky blue.
Its emblem joins symbols of peace from two cultures.
It replaced a red flag that looked too communist.
oman: A red hoist band with a dagger over crossed swords, beside white, red and green bands.
Its emblem shows a traditional curved dagger.
Introduced in 1970 by a sultan who ruled for fifty years.
ontario: A red ensign with a shield of three gold maple leaves under St George's Cross.
Adopted in 1965 to keep a link with a flag the country had just dropped.
A neighbouring province's flag is similar, with a bison.
oregon: Navy blue with gold 'STATE OF OREGON' and a shield on the front, and a beaver on the back.
The only US state flag with two different sides.
ottoman-empire: A white crescent and five-pointed star on red, from an empire that ended in 1922.
Its star was reduced from eight to five points during a reform era.
A republic kept its design almost unchanged.
pakistan: Dark green with a white crescent and star, and a white band at the hoist.
Its white band represents religious minorities.
Adopted three days before its country became independent.
Based on the flag of a political party founded in 1906.
palau: A yellow disc set slightly toward the hoist on light blue.
Its disc is the full moon, a good time for fishing and planting.
It looks like an Asian sun flag recoloured.
palestine: Black, white and green bands with a red triangle at the hoist, no emblem.
Identical to a neighbour's flag except for a missing star.
Based on the flag of a 1916 revolt against the Ottomans.
panama: Four quarters: white with a blue star, red, blue, and white with a red star.
Its blue and red stand for two rival political parties.
Sewn by the wife of its country's first president in 1903.
papua-new-guinea: A diagonal split of red with a yellow bird of paradise and black with the Southern Cross.
Adopted four years before independence from Australia.
paraguay: Red, white and blue horizontal bands with a different emblem on each side.
Its reverse shows a lion guarding a liberty cap.
Its front shows a star named after the month of its independence.
pennsylvania: Two black horses supporting a shield with a ship, a plough and wheat, under an eagle, on blue.
Its motto is 'Virtue, Liberty and Independence'.
peru: Red, white and red vertical bands of equal width.
A legend says flamingos inspired its colours.
Its state version adds a shield with a vicuña and a cornucopia.
Its colours were chosen by a liberator from across the Andes in 1820.
philippines: Blue over red with a white hoist triangle holding a gold sun and three stars.
Flown with red on top in wartime.
Its sun's eight rays stand for provinces that rose against a colonial power.
Designed by a general in exile in Hong Kong.
pitcairn-islands: A blue ensign with a green triangle, an anchor, a Bible and a wheelbarrow.
Its anchor and Bible come from a famous mutiny ship.
The least populous jurisdiction in the world.
poland: White over red, two horizontal bands.
Its colours come from a white eagle on a red shield.
Declared the national colours during an uprising in 1831.
Two other countries use the same colours upside down.
portugal: Green at the hoist, red in the fly, with a shield over a gold armillary sphere.
Its sphere was the emblem of a king of the Age of Discoveries.
Five small blue shields on it are linked to a legend of a 12th-century battle.
It replaced a blue and white royal flag after a revolution in 1910.
prince-edward-island: A gold lion above a large oak and three saplings, with a red and white border.
Its three saplings are three counties.
Adopted for the centenary of a conference that led to a country's founding.
puerto-rico: Red and white stripes with a blue hoist triangle and white star.
Its colours are those of a neighbouring island's flag, reversed.
Displaying it was once a crime under a 1948 law.
qatar: Maroon with a white hoist band and a zigzag edge of nine points.
The only national flag more than twice as wide as it is tall.
Its colour is said to come from red dye darkening in desert sun.
A nearby kingdom has a similar red flag with five points.
qing-dynasty: A blue dragon on yellow reaching for a red pearl.
The first national flag of a vast empire, created for naval and diplomatic use.
Replaced by a five-stripe flag after a revolution in 1911–1912.
quebec: A white cross on blue with four white fleurs-de-lis.
Its lilies recall a French royal heritage in North America.
Adopted in 1948 to replace the Union Flag over a provincial assembly.
queensland: A blue ensign with a light blue disc holding a Maltese cross and crown.
Its state is named after a queen.
Its cross is linked to a military medal.
region-of-murcia: Crimson with four gold castles and seven crowns.
Its crowns stand for royal privileges.
republic-of-the-congo: A yellow diagonal band between green and red triangles.
Replaced by a communist emblem flag from 1970 to 1991.
Its capital faces another capital across a river.
rhineland-palatinate: The German tricolour with a shield in the canton showing a cross, a wheel and a lion.
Its crown is made of vine leaves.
rhode-island: A gold anchor ringed by thirteen stars on white, above the word 'HOPE'.
Its motto is a single word.
Its anchor comes from a biblical verse about hope.
romania: Blue, yellow and red vertical bands.
Almost identical to a Central African flag.
Its communist emblem was cut out by protesters in 1989.
Two principalities united under it in 1859.
russia: White, blue and red horizontal bands, with no emblem.
Traditionally linked to a tsar who studied shipbuilding abroad.
It disappeared for over seventy years and returned during a failed coup.
Its colours became the basis for a family of flags named after an ethnolinguistic group.
rwanda: A double-height light blue band over yellow and green, with a golden sun in the upper fly.
Adopted in 2001 to promote national reconciliation.
Its predecessor had a large letter in the centre.
saarland: The German tricolour with a quartered shield of lions, a cross and eagles.
Its region was a French protectorate until 1956.
sahrawi-arab-democratic-republic: Black, white and green bands with a red hoist triangle and a red crescent and star.
Its state is an African Union member but controls only part of its claimed territory.
Like Palestine's flag with a crescent and star added.
saint-helena: A blue ensign with a plover above a sailing ship between cliffs.
Its island was Napoleon's final place of exile.
saint-kitts-and-nevis: A black diagonal band edged in yellow with two white stars, between green and red triangles.
The flag of the smallest country in the Americas.
Designed by a student for independence in 1983.
saint-lucia: Light blue with a black triangle edged in white and a gold triangle in front.
Its triangles evoke twin volcanic peaks.
Designed by a local painter in 1967.
saint-pierre-and-miquelon: Blue with a yellow ship and three small regional flags at the hoist.
Its small flags honour Basque, Breton and Norman settlers.
The last remnant of New France.
saint-vincent-and-the-grenadines: Blue, wide gold and green vertical bands with three green diamonds in a V.
Its diamonds make the first letter of its main island's name.
Its islands are called the 'Gems of the Antilles'.
samoa: Red with a blue canton holding five white stars of the Southern Cross.
The flag of the first Pacific island nation to become independent.
Its country skipped a whole day in 2011 by moving across the date line.
san-marino: White over light blue with a shield of three towers on three peaks.
A tiny republic surrounded by another country claims founding in 301.
sao-tome-and-principe: Green, yellow and green bands with a red hoist triangle and two black stars.
Its two stars are two islands on the equator.
Its yellow is linked to cocoa.
saskatchewan: Green over gold with a shield at the hoist and a red lily in the fly.
Its halves are northern forest and southern grain.
Chosen from over 4,000 entries in a 1968 competition.
saudi-arabia: A green flag with white Arabic calligraphy above a horizontal sword.
It is never flown at half-mast because of the words on it.
It is made double-sided so its inscription reads correctly from both sides.
Its inscription is a declaration of religious faith.
saxony: White over green, two horizontal bands.
Its colours belonged to a dynasty that ruled for over 800 years.
A German Free State with Dresden as capital.
saxony-anhalt: Yellow over black with arms showing a bear on a wall.
Its colours are the reverse of a south-western state's.
Its bear comes from a former duchy.
canton-of-schaffhausen: A black ram leaping on yellow.
Its animal is a pun on its name.
Home to Europe's largest waterfall by volume.
schleswig-holstein: Blue, white and red horizontal bands.
Its colours date from a 19th-century uprising against Danish rule.
canton-of-schwyz: A red square with a small white cross in the corner.
It gave its name to an entire country.
A founding canton whose banner became a national flag.
scotland: A white diagonal cross on blue.
A legend says it appeared in the sky before a 9th-century battle.
Its saint was crucified on an X-shaped cross.
senegal: Green, yellow and red vertical bands with a green star in the centre.
It replaced a human figure from a short-lived federation in 1960.
Its neighbour's flag is the same without the star.
serbia: Red, blue and white bands with a crowned double-headed white eagle.
Its shield shows a cross with four firesteels.
Its colours are those of a Slavic power's flag turned upside down.
seychelles: Five coloured bands fanning out from the lower hoist corner.
The only national flag with bands radiating from a corner.
Adopted in 1996 with the return of multi-party politics.
sierra-leone: Green, white and blue horizontal bands.
Its blue stands for a great natural harbour.
Its colours came from a coat of arms granted the year before independence.
singapore: Red over white with a white crescent and five stars in the upper hoist.
Its five stars stand for democracy, peace, progress, justice and equality.
Its crescent represents a young nation rising, not a religion.
Designed in 1959 for self-government, kept through a brief federation.
sint-maarten: Red over blue with a white hoist triangle holding a shield with a courthouse and a pelican.
Its island is shared with a French territory.
slovakia: White, blue and red bands with a shield showing a white double cross on blue hills.
Its three hills are traditionally named after three mountain ranges.
Adopted months before its federation split peacefully in 1993.
slovenia: White, blue and red bands with a shield showing a three-peaked mountain and three gold stars.
Its stars come from a medieval family of counts.
Often confused with a neighbour whose name differs by a few letters.
socialist-federal-republic-of-yugoslavia: Blue, white and red bands with a large red star edged in gold across them.
Partisans added its star during the Second World War.
Its federation broke apart in 1991–1992, leaving two republics to keep the plain tricolour.
Its six republics each had their own star-bearing flags.
solomon-islands: A thin yellow diagonal between blue with five white stars and green.
Its stars stood for five districts, though there are now nine provinces.
Adopted a year before independence in 1978.
canton-of-solothurn: Its town is famous for the number eleven.
somalia: A white star on a light blue field.
Its star's points stand for five regions where one people live.
Its blue honours the United Nations.
somaliland: Green, white and red bands with white script in the green and a black star.
Its black star mourns a failed union.
It declared independence in 1991 but lacks recognition.
south-africa: A green horizontal Y separates red and blue bands, with a black triangle at the hoist.
Six colours, no emblem, designed by a state herald in a matter of weeks.
First raised on the day of its country's first fully democratic election.
It replaced an orange-white-blue flag carrying three miniature flags.
south-australia: A blue ensign with a black and white bird on a branch inside a yellow disc.
Its bird is known by an old name, the piping shrike.
Its disc is the rising sun.
south-carolina: A white palmetto tree and crescent on indigo blue.
Its tree honours a fort whose logs absorbed cannonballs.
Its crescent comes from soldiers' cap badges in 1775.
south-dakota: A seal ringed by gold sun rays on sky blue, naming a famous mountain sculpture.
It changed its nickname from 'The Sunshine State' in 1992.
Its motto is 'Under God the people rule'.
south-korea: A red and blue yin-yang circle on white with four black trigrams.
Its corner symbols stand for heaven, earth, water and fire.
A diplomat flew it on a mission abroad in 1882, the year before it became official.
It was banned in its own country for 35 years of occupation.
south-sudan: Black, red and green bands edged in white, with a blue hoist triangle and a yellow star.
The flag of the newest UN member state.
Its blue triangle stands for a great river.
south-vietnam: Yellow with three thin red horizontal stripes.
Its stripes stand for the three regions of a country it claimed in full.
It is still flown by communities abroad as a 'heritage and freedom' flag.
Its state ended with the fall of its capital in April 1975.
soviet-union: Red with a gold hammer and sickle under a star outlined in gold.
Lowered from the Kremlin for the last time on 25 December 1991.
Its reverse side was officially plain red.
Its tools stood for industrial workers and peasants.
spain: A yellow band twice as wide as the red bands above and below it, with a crowned shield toward the hoist.
Two pillars on it carry a motto meaning 'further beyond'.
Chosen by a king in 1785 to make his warships easier to identify at sea.
A republic in the 1930s replaced its lower band with purple.
sri-lanka: A gold lion with a sword on maroon, with green and saffron stripes beside it.
Its corner leaves come from the tree of the Buddha's enlightenment.
Its lion comes from the banner of a highland kingdom that fell in 1815.
Two stripes were added in 1951 to represent minorities.
canton-of-st-gallen: A white bundle of rods with an axe on green.
A canton created in 1803 under Napoleon.
styria: White over green, two horizontal bands.
Its colours come from a fire-breathing panther.
sudan: Red, white and black bands with a green triangle at the hoist.
It replaced a blue, yellow and green flag in 1970.
Its black represents its country's name.
suriname: Green, white, red, white and green bands with a yellow star in the red.
Its predecessor had five stars joined by an ellipse.
Adopted at independence from the Netherlands in 1975.
sweden: A yellow Nordic cross on a blue field.
Its colours come from three golden crowns on a royal shield.
For six decades its canton held a mark nicknamed after a fish dish.
A legend claims a king saw its cross in the sky before a crusade.
switzerland: A white cross on a red square, not touching the edges.
One of only two square national flags.
Reverse its colours and you get a humanitarian emblem founded in its country.
Derived from the banner of one of three founding cantons.
syria: Green, white and black bands with three red stars across the white band.
Flown by an opposition movement for thirteen years before becoming national again.
First adopted under a French Mandate in 1932.
Its stars once stood for three districts, including Aleppo.
taiwan: Red with a blue canton holding a white twelve-rayed sun.
It competes at the Olympics under a different flag with a plum blossom.
Its sun's rays stand for the twelve months and twelve two-hour periods.
Adopted for all of China in 1928.
tajikistan: Red, a double-width white band, and green, with a gold crown under seven stars.
Its crown refers to a word for crown in its own national name.
Its capital once had the world's tallest flagpole.
tanzania: A black diagonal band edged in yellow, between green and light blue triangles.
It merges the flags of two states that united in 1964.
Its country's name is a blend of two names.
tasmania: A blue ensign with a red lion on a white disc.
The flag of Australia's island state.
Its state was once called Van Diemen's Land.
tennessee: Red with a blue disc containing three white stars and a narrow blue bar at the fly.
Its three stars stand for three Grand Divisions.
Its fly bar was added so it would not look too red when limp.
texas: A blue hoist band with a white star, beside white over red.
It flew over an independent republic from 1839 to 1845.
A South American flag is often mixed up with it.
thailand: Red, white, blue, white, red stripes with a double-height blue centre.
It replaced a flag with a white elephant.
A king is said to have designed it after seeing a flag hung upside down.
Its three colours stand for 'Nation, Religion, King'.
the-bahamas: Aquamarine, gold and aquamarine bands with a black triangle at the hoist.
Its gold stands for beaches and its blue for clear seas.
Adopted in July 1973 for an archipelago of hundreds of islands.
the-gambia: Red, white-edged blue, and green horizontal bands.
Its blue band is a river running through a narrow country.
Its country is almost entirely surrounded by one neighbour.
canton-of-thurgau: A diagonal white and green split with two yellow lions.
A canton on Lake Constance known for cider.
thuringia: White over red, two horizontal bands.
The reverse of a neighbouring German state's colours.
Its state arms show a striped lion with eight stars.
timor-leste: Red with a yellow triangle and a black triangle holding a tilted white star.
Raised in 1975 and again in 2002 after years of occupation.
The flag of the first new state of the 21st century.
togo: Green and yellow stripes with a red canton holding a white star.
Its proportions approximate the golden ratio.
Its five stripes stand for five regions.
tokelau: Dark blue with a yellow canoe and four white stars.
Its canoe represents a journey toward self-determination.
Its three atolls voted twice on self-government.
tonga: Red with a white canton holding a red cross.
Its constitution says it may never be changed.
Its king chose it to express his Christian faith in 1875.
transnistria: Red with a green band and a gold hammer and sickle.
It keeps the flag of a Soviet republic.
Recognised by no UN member, it split from a former Soviet republic in 1990.
trinidad-and-tobago: Red with a black diagonal band edged in white.
Its three colours are said to stand for earth, water and fire.
Chosen by an independence committee in 1962.
tunisia: A red crescent and star inside a white disc on a red field.
Introduced in 1831 after a fleet was destroyed at Navarino.
Used through a French protectorate and into independence.
turkey: A white crescent and star slightly toward the hoist on a red field.
Its star once had eight points, until a 19th-century reform era.
A legend links it to a moon reflected in pools of blood after a battle.
Its geometry was set by a law of 1936, inherited from an empire.
turkmenistan: Green with a red hoist band of carpet patterns, olive branches, and a white crescent with five stars.
Its band shows designs from five tribes' carpets.
Olive branches were added for its UN-recognised neutrality.
turks-and-caicos-islands: A blue ensign with a gold shield showing a conch, a lobster and a cactus.
Its islands are named after a cactus shaped like a fez.
An old badge mistakenly drew salt piles as igloos.
tuvalu: A light blue ensign with the Union Flag and nine yellow stars forming a map.
Its country's name means 'eight standing together'.
It was replaced in 1995 and brought back in 1997.
tyrol: White over red with a red eagle wearing a green wreath.
Its eagle is shared with a province across the Italian border.
uganda: Black, yellow and red stripes repeated twice, with a crane in a white disc.
Its bird stands on one leg to show forward movement.
Its crane was the badge of a British protectorate.
ukraine: Blue over yellow in two equal horizontal bands.
Popularly read as a clear sky above fields of wheat.
Its colours come from a golden lion on a medieval kingdom's arms.
Banned for decades and restored in 1992.
united-arab-emirates: A vertical red band at the hoist, with green, white and black horizontal bands.
Designed by a 19-year-old in a competition for a new federation in 1971.
Its seven member states each keep their own flags.
united-kingdom: Three national crosses, one upright and two diagonal, overlaid on a blue field.
It has a correct way up because its diagonal crosses are offset.
One constituent country is not represented on it at all.
It sits in the canton of several other national flags in Oceania.
united-states: Thirteen horizontal stripes of red and white and a blue canton full of white stars.
Its canton has been redesigned more than twenty times, a new version each time the federation grew.
A star is added on the Fourth of July after a new member joins.
A version with fifteen stripes inspired a national anthem written during a bombardment in 1814.
united-states-virgin-islands: White with a yellow eagle between the letters V and I.
Its eagle holds three arrows for three islands.
Its islands were bought from Denmark in 1917.
upper-austria: White over red with a shield of a gold eagle and stripes, under an archducal hat.
An Austrian state whose capital is Linz.
canton-of-uri: A black bull's head with a nose ring on yellow.
A founding canton, home of the William Tell legend.
uruguay: Nine white and blue stripes with a golden sun with a face in the canton.
Its sun has sixteen rays, half as many as its neighbour's.
Its stripes stand for nine original departments.
It is one of three official national flags of its country.
utah: A gold beehive in a blue hexagon, with white mountains above and red rock below.
Adopted in 2024 after a public redesign.
Its red band represents desert canyons.
uzbekistan: Light blue, white and green bands with red edging, a white crescent and twelve stars.
Its twelve stars stand for months and the zodiac.
Its blue was the colour of a 14th-century conqueror's banner.
canton-of-valais: White and red halves with thirteen counterchanged stars.
valencian-community: Red and gold stripes with a crowned blue band at the hoist.
Like Catalonia's flag with a royal blue band added.
vanuatu: Red and green divided by a yellow Y, with a boar's tusk and fern leaves in a black triangle.
Its fern fronds number the members of the first parliament.
Its country was once ruled jointly by two European powers.
vatican-city: A square flag of yellow and white halves with crossed keys and a triple crown.
Its keys refer to a biblical promise made to an apostle.
One of two square national flags.
canton-of-vaud: White over green with a French motto in gold.
Its canton freed itself from Bernese rule in 1798.
Home of the International Olympic Committee.
venezuela: Yellow, blue and red bands with an arc of eight white stars.
An eighth star was added in 2006.
Its colours were first flown by Francisco de Miranda in 1806.
Its blue is said to be the sea separating it from Spain.
vermont: A coat of arms with a pine, a cow and wheat in front of green mountains, on blue.
Its state was an independent republic before joining the Union in 1791.
victoria: A blue ensign with the Southern Cross under a crown.
The first Australian colony to fly the Southern Cross.
Its crown was changed after a coronation in 1953.
vienna: Red over white, two horizontal bands, shared by three states.
The flag of a capital that is also a state.
vietnam: A single large yellow star centred on red.
First used in an uprising against French colonial rule in 1940.
The flag of a former southern state, yellow with three red stripes, is still flown by communities abroad.
virginia: A woman with a spear standing over a fallen tyrant, on blue.
Its motto means 'Thus always to tyrants'.
wales: A red dragon on white over green.
Its country is not represented on its union's flag.
Its colours come from a royal house that won the Battle of Bosworth.
wallis-and-futuna: Red with a French tricolour in the canton and a white cross of four triangles.
Its territory contains three traditional kingdoms.
Its cross came from the flag of a Polynesian kingdom.
washington: A portrait of a man in a gold ring on dark green.
The only US state flag showing a president.
The only US state flag with a green field.
west-virginia: A white field with a blue border and arms showing a farmer and a miner beside a dated rock.
Its date marks statehood during a civil war.
Its motto means 'Mountaineers are always free'.
western-australia: A blue ensign with a black swan on a yellow disc.
Its swan was turned around in 1953.
Its capital lies on a river named after the bird.
wisconsin: A coat of arms with a sailor, a miner and a badger, with the state name and 1848, on blue.
Its crest is a burrowing mammal.
wyoming: A white bison on blue inside white and red borders.
Its emblem is branded on an animal's flank.
Its seal celebrates the first territory to give women the vote.
yemen: Plain red, white and black horizontal bands.
Adopted when two states united in 1990.
Egypt's and Iraq's flags are similar but add emblems.
yukon: Green, white and blue vertical bands with a coat of arms above purple flowers.
Its arms are topped by a sled dog.
Its territory saw a famous gold rush.
zambia: Green with an orange eagle in flight above red, black and orange stripes in the lower fly.
Unusually, all its symbols are at the fly end.
zimbabwe: Green, yellow, red and black stripes with a white triangle holding a bird and a red star.
Its bird was carved in soapstone at a medieval ruined city.
canton-of-zug: White with a broad blue horizontal band.
A small Swiss canton known for low taxes.
canton-of-zurich: A square flag split diagonally into white and blue.
The flag of Switzerland's largest city and its canton.
